content.title: Knicks 130, Pelicans 125: Zion Williamson 32 points | Postgame wrap | New Orleans Pelicans
content.text: New Orleans interim head coach James Borrego has told rookie center Derik Queen that pieces of the 21-year-old’s unique skill set can be a major asset for the Pelicans, saying Queen “rebounding and starting a (fast) break (by dribbling up the floor) is our best offense.”Meanwhile, Executive Vice President of Basketball Operations Joe Dumars – a Hall of Fame player as a Detroit Pistons guard – has explained to Queen that double-digit rebounding games should be exceptionally common for the University of Maryland product. So common that, as a smiling Queen described after Monday’s morning shootaround, “(Dumars) just told me recently, if I get under 10 rebounds (in a game), that should be a crime.”Currently No. 3 on NBA.com’s Rookie Ladder (behind only Cooper Flagg and Kon Knueppel), Queen has been making his head coach and the team’s lead basketball executive very pleased lately. Entering Monday’s 7 p.m. home game vs. New York (GCSEN on TV; WWL on radio), Queen has averaged 9.5 rebounds (and 16.8 points on 53 percent shooting) over his last six games. He’s notched double-doubles in four of those contests, including 21 points and 11 rebounds Saturday vs. Phoenix, his second 20-10 outing of 2025-26.“Having double-doubles is always a goal of mine,” Queen said. “It’s something I look at every day. Coach JB always says me rebounding and starting a break gives us a chance of getting a great shot.”Other notes from shootaround:Asked if he’s thought about the Rookie of the Year award, with Queen considered a top-three candidate by many NBA analysts, the Baltimore native said he’s trying to focus on his own play and letting that speak for itself.“I’ve just got to keep progressing, keep trying to win games, keep being the best player I can be,” Queen said. “(If I do that), I think I’ll have results.”New York Scouting ReportOffensive efficiency (rank): 121.1 (3)Defensive efficiency (rank): 114.3 (15)Net rating (rank): +6.8 (4)Streak: Won 2 (vs. Cleveland, at Atlanta)Go-to guy: Currently fourth on NBA.com’s Race to the MVP Ladder, point guard Jalen Brunson is the league’s seventh-leading scorer at 29.5 points per game. The crafty southpaw is also No. 17 in assists average (6.4).On the rise: Logging important minutes at PG behind Brunson lately, second-year pro Tyler Kolek has seen a drastic increase in his role. Kolek emerged as a vital contributor during New York’s run to the 2025 NBA Cup title, with 14 points in the championship game vs. San Antonio.In the clutch: New York has played a low number of clutch games, going 7-5. Not surprisingly, Brunson is again the team’s most reliable crunch-time performer, posting a Knicks-best 26 clutch points this season. He’s 4/8 on threes, including a dagger trey Saturday to help beat Atlanta 128-125.Three-point attack: One of the league’s most dangerous perimeter-shooting teams, the Knicks rank fourth in makes per game (15.1) and fourth in percentage (38.2). The Pelicans are now last in makes (10.6) and No. 27 in percentage (34.0).Previous Game Starting LineupsNEW YORK (22-9)Saturday win at AtlantaJalen Brunson, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby, Mohamed Diawara, Karl-Anthony TownsNotes: Kolek (ankle) is questionable. Josh Hart (ankle), Mitchell Robinson (ankle) and Landry Shamet (shoulder) are out. Miles McBride (ankle) is probable. … Diawara, a rookie from France, made the second start of his NBA career in the victory over the Hawks. … Benefiting from consecutive Detroit losses on a Pistons road trip, New York has now pulled to within 1.5 games of the top spot in the Eastern Conference. If the season ended right now, the second-seeded Knicks would face the winner of the 7-8 play-in game (Cleveland at Miami). … On Dec. 16, New York joined the Lakers (2023) and Milwaukee (2024) among the three franchises that have captured an NBA Cup championship.NEW ORLEANS (8-25)Saturday loss vs. PhoenixJeremiah Fears, Bryce McGowens, Trey Murphy, Saddiq Bey, Derik QueenNotes: Jose Alvarado is out due to a two-game league suspension. The backup point guard will also miss Wednesday’s game at Chicago. Herb Jones (ankle) and Dejounte Murray (Achilles) are out. Trey Alexander and Hunter Dickinson are out due to G League duty. … New Orleans is 5.5 games behind No. 10 Portland in the West. The Pelicans will host the Trail Blazers this week on Friday. … The Pelicans are 4-4 this season against the East (including 3-2 in the Smoothie King Center), but 4-21 vs. the West. They’ve faced every West opponent except Utah and Sacramento. … New Orleans will wrap up the 2025 calendar Wednesday by visiting Chicago, seeking a 3-0 sweep in the season series over the Bulls.
